subject: ventures/einvoice-preflight
professional: an e-invoicing integration consultant who signs off ERP output for Peppol/XRechnung/EN 16931; first checks: are the fix figures right to the cent, does the repair leave a correct invoice alone, and does the Python CLI a pipeline runs give the same verdict as the page on the same file

evidence.correctness: Recomputed by hand through checkInvoice/repairInvoice (scratchpad probe.mjs): 100.00@19% + 50.00@7% = 22.50 tax; with 23.50 stated both the page engine and the CLI say 'Set tax to 22.50' (INV-018) plus INV-037 (no per-rate breakdown, EN 16931 BG-23). The 10^13 IDR invoice (9,876,543,210,987.65 x 11% = 1,086,419,753,208.6415 -> .64, gross .29) draws no finding and repairInvoice changes nothing. Half-up tie 1.50 x 19% = 0.285 -> 0.29 accepted. NEW: python-stdnum 2.2 (no.mva, ch.vat) against the CLI on 3,000 random NO/CH numbers (263 valid): before this PR the CLI answered INV-022 'unrecognized country prefix' for every one of them as vat_id, correct numbers included, and checked none given as id; after the port 3,000/3,000 agree with stdnum and with vat.mjs.
evidence.completeness: Page, Node API and CLI paths exercised above on JSON; the parity harness's documented gaps (PDF envelope checks, profile options, fix texts) remain as NEXT.md says; NO/CH VAT removed from that list by this PR.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 2,493 tests, 2,342 pass, 0 fail, 151 skipped (corpora not fetched), 9.7 s. PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 451 pass. Mutants: NO weight 2->3 in vat.py caught by the new NorwaySwitzerlandTest; the 1e15 large-amount threshold widened to 1e17 caught by large-amount-rounding.test.mjs; Math.round -> Math.floor in the shared cent rounding caught by the full suite. Before this PR no Python test touched NO or CH at all.
evidence.craft: Read numbers.mjs, checks.mjs:28-40, breakdown.mjs:20-45, adjustment.mjs, linenet.mjs:1-20 and vat.py. On arrival the half-up-to-cent helper was four identical copies (checks, breakdown, adjustment, linenet) plus variants at other precisions (cfdi.mjs:170, creditlink.mjs:39, repair-ubl.mjs:41/56); this PR folds the four into numbers.mjs. README.md is now 403,315 bytes of dated run log (398 KB at the prior audit), so craft stays 2.
evidence.claims: checks.mjs:1-7 and README:1250 said NO/CH VAT is 'JS only': true, but the consequence was understated (the CLI rejected correct NO/CH numbers, not merely skipped them); both lines and NEXT.md:35 updated by this PR. index.html 'Prefer a pipeline?' says the CLI matches the page on the 42 shipped files, which none of them exercise NO/CH, so it held as written. INV-038 fix text now formatted (breakdown.mjs:135 formatCents).
evidence.fitness: A pipeline team checking a Norwegian or Swiss supplier's invoices through the CLI saw a blocking INV-022 on a correct vat_id; after this PR the CLI verdict matches the page. The page user's job was unaffected.
evidence.domain: Norway organisasjonsnummer (Brønnøysund mod 11, weights 3,2,7,6,5,4,3,2, remainder 10 never issued, optional MVA suffix) and Swiss UID (CHE + 8 digits + mod-11 check, weights 5,4,3,2,7,6,5,4, MWST/TVA/IVA suffix) as python-stdnum implements them; EN 16931 BR-CO-14/BR-CO-17 rounding as before. INV-005 on a name-only buyer remains stricter than EN 16931 (BT-46/47/48 optional), deliberate and documented.

defects.what: The Python CLI answered a blocking INV-022 'unrecognized country prefix' for every Norwegian or Swiss vat_id, correct ones included, and never checked one given as id; the prior audit recorded this as 'passes a mistyped NO/CH number'. Fixed in this PR (vat.py ports vat.mjs's mod-11 rules; 3,000/3,000 agree with python-stdnum).
README.md is 403,315 bytes of dated run log; rounding variants at other precisions remain in cfdi.mjs, creditlink.mjs and repair-ubl.mjs.
Prior defect 4 persists: a buyer known by name alone draws a blocking INV-005 though BT-46/47/48 are optional in EN 16931 (deliberate, documented).

verdict: Sixth audit; meets the bar again. Both defects PR #19982 marked fixed are closed: the 10^13 IDR invoice draws nothing and repairs to itself, and the INV-038 figure is formatted. Hand recomputations of a mixed-rate total, a half-cent tie and the large IDR invoice all agree, in the page engine and the CLI. The open NO/CH defect was worse than recorded: the CLI rejected every correct Norwegian or Swiss VAT id as an unknown prefix. This PR ports the check digits (3,000 of 3,000 random numbers agree with python-stdnum and vat.mjs) and folds the four identical cent-rounding copies into numbers.mjs; scores are before those fixes. Craft stays 2 for the 403 KB run-log README; the name-only buyer INV-005 stays deliberate.
